newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong set to be hit head-on by tropical storm.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong set to be hit head-on by tropical storm.

text.p: A typhoon bore down on Hong Kong on Saturday, threatening to be the worst for years, severely disrupting air traffic and shipping and forcing emergency measures.

The territory's 6.4 million people rushed supermarkets to stock up as rain pelted down or scurried for cover and battened down hatches for a long stay indoors. Roads were clogged as workers headed home.
Nearby Portuguese-ruled Macau also braced for Typhoon Victor to hit, after it had caused disruption to air and sea traffic.

The Hong Kong Observatory hoisted typhoon warning signal eight at noon (0400 GMT), which means that winds with speeds of 63 to 117 km an hour (40 to 74 mph) are expected. Macau issued the same warning signal an hour earlier.
Hong Kong said a higher tropical cyclone warning signal may have to be hoisted later and a spokesman at the observatory said it was possible that Victor would make a direct hit on Hong Kong.

At 4 p.m. (0800 GMT) the storm was centred about 120 km (70 miles) south of Hong Kong and forecast to move north at about 18 km per hour (11 mph) towards the Pearl River estuary, the observatory said.
Victor was expected to make landfall near the estuary later this evening. Hong Kong is located at the far eastern edge of the estuary, while Macau is located at the western edge.

Victor, threatening to come closest to Hong Kong of any typhoon in recent years, forced 83 flights leaving or arriving in Hong Kong to be diverted, delayed or cancelled, a spokesman for Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department told Reuters.
Ferry services to outlying islands and to Macau were cancelled because of the bad weather. Macau's small international airport was shut due to the bad weather.
Hong Kong's TVB news said minor flooding occurred in some areas of Macau.
The Hong Kong government urged people to take precautions, board up windows and doors and advised workers to go home. Schools were closed and government employees sent home.
